result:
The final answer of 1/2 is incorrect.

The proposed construction, taking all x with v_{p₁}(x) even, avoids every pair {x, p₁x}. That is a much stronger condition than the problem requires. The problem only forbids the full set {n, p₁n, …, p_rn}, so a larger set is possible.

A better construction uses the weight w(x) = Σ i·v_{p_i}(x) mod (r+1). Let B be the set of x with w(x) ≡ 0, and let A be the complement of B.

For any n, the elements n, p₁n, …, p_rn have weights w(n), w(n)+1, …, w(n)+r. These cover all residues mod r+1, so exactly one of them lies in B. Hence A contains no forbidden configuration.

The set B has density about 1/(r+1) among S-smooth integers up to X, so A has density about r/(r+1). This gives lim F_S(X)/Ψ_S(X) ≥ r/(r+1), which is at least 2/3 for r ≥ 2. That already exceeds 1/2, so the claimed limit cannot be right.

The "known result" cited in the solution was not justified. The limit is likely r/(r+1), though I have only shown the lower bound.

VERDICT: REJECT
